description: Global Fishing Watch publishes vessel activity data derived from the automatic identification system (AIS), combined with vessel monitoring system data shared by some governments, and from satellite imagery. Its API functions cover apparent fishing effort for nearly 70,000 AIS vessels, vessel search and identity across more than 40 public registries, fishing events, encounters and possible transshipment, loitering, port visits, vessel insights, and SAR vessel detections and offshore fixed infrastructure classified with deep learning, and bulk export of worldwide activity as CSV or JSON. Datasets for download include fishing effort, transshipment, anchorages and vessel identity, and monthly, daily and yearly SAR detection layers are also shared on ArcGIS Living Atlas. Coverage is global, over the ocean. Data and APIs are free of charge for non-commercial use after a free registration, an API token and agreement to the terms of use with attribution. Caveats: AIS is self-reported and not carried by all vessels, the focus is fishing and industrial vessels, and commercial use is not allowed. It supports exposure of port and shipping activity, monitoring of vessel traffic changes after disruptions and mapping of offshore infrastructure. It complements the Marine Cadastre AIS data and is related to the Danish Maritime Authority AIS data.
